clue.text: Possibly making up a verse on spectacular stars

indicators.note: possibly says the letters that follow could be arranged some other way, an anagram signal

explanation.surface: A poet perhaps composing verse about dazzling stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges UP A VERSE ON; 'making' just joins. The sky-gazing surface makes 'making up' look like composing.
explanation.definitionFit: A supernova is a star that explodes and blazes brilliantly, so the plural form names spectacular stellar outbursts.

clue.text: Like being in a mess — a mess indeed!

annotationWithheld.why: Like being in a mess — a mess indeed! (4): no parse found; 'a mess' has five letters with two Ss, so it cannot be anagrammed to the four-letter answer, and no source gives the setter's intended wordplay
annotationWithheld.clue: Like being in a mess — a mess indeed!

clue.text: Those past reforming may appear very sharp

indicators.note: reforming means the letters of the two words are formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: People beyond reform may look very smart and well turned out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reforming' rearranges THOSE PAST. 'Sharp' looks like smart dress, but here it means promptly, as in 'at ten sharp'.
explanation.definitionFit: Very sharp as in very prompt, at top speed: the adverb means with all possible haste.

clue.text: Approach from Russian leaders that play with words when re tired

parts.note: the leading two letters of the word Russian

indicators.note: printed with a space, retired means drawn back, so the word for a play on words is read backwards

parts.note: a pun is a play on words

explanation.surface: A Russian leader's speech full of wordplay, delivered when worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 're tired' is 'retired' with a space put in by the printer; retired means drawn back, so it turns the word for wordplay round. 'Russian leaders' means the word's first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-up is the approach a bowler or jumper takes, or the period of preparation leading to an event.

clue.text: An area of fruit or vegetable

parts.note: chard is a leafy vegetable, Swiss chard

explanation.surface: A choice between growing fruit or vegetables on a plot.
explanation.definitionFit: An area planted with fruit trees is the standard sense of the word.

clue.text: Learn as working to bring out a magazine

indicators.note: working means the letters are worked into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Studying hard in order to publish a periodical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges LEARN AS. 'Magazine' suggests a periodical, but it is the military sense: a store of weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: A magazine in its military sense is a store for arms and ammunition, which is what an arsenal is.

clue.text: Performs before Romans

definitions.meaning: does or carries out, a verb
in the New Testament the book of ... comes immediately before the Epistle to the Romans

explanation.surface: Someone putting on a show in front of an audience of ancient Romans.
explanation.definitionFit: To perform is to do, and the Acts of the Apostles is the Bible book placed directly ahead of Romans.

clue.text: To edge into church is wrong

indicators.note: into means the word for an edge goes inside the letters for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: Sidling into a church service is improper behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' signals the container; 'To' is only a link. 'Wrong' is a noun here, an offence, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrong as a noun is an offence or misdeed, the same as a criminal act.

clue.text: Give voice about small number adding sugar

indicators.note: about means the verb for giving voice surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: to give voice is to sing
wee is Scottish for small
ten is a number

explanation.surface: Singing about a small number of spoonfuls of sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals that the singing word goes around the other two pieces; 'Give voice' looks like speaking up, but it means sing.
explanation.definitionFit: Adding sugar to food or drink is the act of making it sweet, a sense the present participle carries directly.

clue.text: Murder as a result of a celebration with port

parts.note: Mass is a celebration of the Eucharist
Acre is a port in northern Israel

explanation.surface: A killing following a party in a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Celebration' suggests a party, but a priest celebrates Mass. Acre is a historic port on the coast of Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: A massacre is a mass killing, slaughter on a large scale, so murder works as a definition.

clue.text: Many a boy will become an artisan

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Lots of boys will grow up to be skilled tradesmen.
explanation.walkthrough: M for 'Many' is a crossword convention: the Roman numeral for a thousand stands for a large number.
explanation.definitionFit: A mason is a craftsman who works in stone, a classic skilled artisan.

clue.text: Found a team spurned

parts.note: to found metal is to cast it in a mould
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A team was established and then rejected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like the past of 'find' or 'establish', but it is the metalworking verb: to cast.
explanation.definitionFit: Spurned means rejected or discarded, which is what being thrown away like this means.

clue.text: Honour a simple man of the cloth

parts.note: CH is Companion of Honour, a British order
plain means simple

explanation.surface: Honouring a humble clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A man of the cloth is a clergyman, and a chaplain is a clergyman attached to an institution such as a regiment or hospital.

clue.text: The writer in the street appears worn-out

indicators.note: in means the writing tool sits inside the abbreviation for street

parts.note: a pen is what writes

explanation.surface: An author spotted on the road looks exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The writer' suggests an author but means the pen; 'in' puts it inside ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Spent means exhausted, used up, with nothing left: worn-out.

clue.text: People suffering some hurt from nonchalant relationships

parts.note: casual means nonchalant, unconcerned
ties are bonds or relationships

explanation.surface: Being hurt by easygoing love affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Casualties are those injured or killed, as in an accident or a battle.

clue.text: Sailors read a note and take flight

parts.note: ABs are able seamen, sailors
to con is to study or read over
D is a musical note

explanation.surface: Seamen read a message and then run away.
explanation.walkthrough: AB is an able seaman. 'Con' in the old sense of studying a text is a crossword favourite for 'read'.
explanation.definitionFit: To abscond is to leave secretly and hurriedly, to run off or flee.

clue.text: Get to know by chance about male artist's backing

parts.note: over can mean about, concerning
he is a male pronoun

indicators.note: backing says the artist's letters are put in back to front

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Learning by chance that a male painter has a sponsor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support for the artist, but it turns RA into AR.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to know something by chance is to catch words not meant for you, as eavesdropping does accidentally.

clue.text: An upholder of the Christian word

definitions.text: An upholder of the Christian word

parts.words: An upholder of the Christian word
parts.note: sounds like a defender of the faith, but it is the stand that literally holds up the Bible in church

explanation.surface: A champion of the Gospel message.
explanation.definitionFit: A lectern is the reading desk that supports the Bible from which lessons are read.

clue.text: A complaint as regards attend, ants

parts.note: to regard is to look at, to eye
a train is a retinue of attendants

explanation.surface: Grumbling about the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regards' looks like 'concerning' but is the verb: looks at. The scan split 'attendants' into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the sense of an ailment: tiredness or soreness from overusing the sight.

clue.text: Employment left, a letter is futile

parts.note: use is employment, as in putting to use
ess is the name of the letter S

explanation.surface: With the job gone, writing a letter is pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Futile means having no effect, serving no purpose.

clue.text: A1 seeds developed in a coastal area

indicators.note: developed means the letters grow into a different arrangement

parts.note: A is the letter itself, and 1 is I, the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: First-rate seeds grown by the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The page's 'Al' is A1, first-class; read as A and I (Roman one), it joins SEEDS to be rearranged by 'developed'.
explanation.definitionFit: The seaside is the land along the coast, a coastal area for holidays.

clue.text: A woman gone to find an illicit place to drink

parts.note: she refers to a woman
been can mean gone, as in having been to a place

explanation.surface: A woman has left to find a secret drinking den.
explanation.walkthrough: A shebeen is an unlicensed Irish or Scottish drinking house.
explanation.definitionFit: A shebeen is an unlicensed bar, a place where alcohol is sold without a licence.

clue.text: To the paying guest accommodated by a fool it's just a temper ary arrangement

indicators.note: accommodated by means the first pieces are housed inside the word for a fool

parts.note: a sap is a fool
taken as written
PG is the abbreviation for paying guest

explanation.surface: A lodger put up by a fool has only a short-term arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodated by' signals the container; the lodger surface makes it read like a rental, and 'temper ary' is the page's split of 'temporary'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopgap is something used for the time being until a proper replacement is found.

clue.text: Wood having some particular characteristic

indicators.note: having some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Timber with a distinctive quality.
explanation.walkthrough: The run straddles particuLAR CHaracteristic.
explanation.definitionFit: Larch is a conifer whose timber is a well-known wood.

clue.text: General carrying the learner's weapon

indicators.note: carrying means the word for general holds the learner letter inside

parts.note: rife means widespread, general
L is the learner plate, a learner driver

explanation.surface: An army general holding a trainee soldier's gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like an army officer, but it is the adjective: widespread. 'carrying' puts L inside RIFE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle is a long-barrelled firearm, a weapon.

clue.text: Renegade given a job tea-blending

parts.note: a post is a job

indicators.note: blending means the letters are mixed up like a blend of tea

explanation.surface: A traitor is assigned the task of mixing teas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blending' rearranges only the drink's three letters; 'given' is a link. The tea-shop picture hides a word for a traitor to a faith.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostate abandons their faith or cause, a renegade or turncoat.

clue.text: A topping building worker!.

parts.note: sounds like praise, topping as old slang for excellent, but this craftsman puts the top on a building

explanation.surface: A splendid builder.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiler lays tiles on roofs, so is the tradesman who covers the top of a house.

clue.text: Only water

definitions.meaning: a lake or pond, a body of standing water

explanation.definitionFit: Mere as an adjective means just or nothing more than; as a noun it is a lake, as in English place names.

clue.text: Blowing up in the apartment in Gateshead

parts.note: a flat is an apartment
read as Gate's head, the opening letter of gate

explanation.surface: Pumping something up in a flat in Gateshead.
explanation.walkthrough: Gateshead is a town in north-east England; read as 'Gate's head' it gives G.
explanation.definitionFit: Blowing up a balloon or tyre is filling it with air.

clue.text: The French way to get a holiday

parts.note: le is French for the
Ave is the abbreviation for avenue, a way

explanation.surface: The French approach to getting time off.
explanation.definitionFit: Leave is time off work, a holiday, as in annual leave.

clue.text: Check a supporter

definitions.meaning: to stop or ... the flow of something
the stalk that holds up a flower or leaf

explanation.definitionFit: To stem is to restrain or halt; a stem is the stalk that bears up a plant's flower.

clue.text: Dealing with creep meant the exercising of self-control

indicators.note: dealing with suggests handling the letters as one deals cards, shuffling them into order

explanation.surface: Coping with a creep required restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dealing with' rearranges CREEP MEANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperance is moderation, restraint in eating and drinking.
